**Paperhue 0.4.2** makes blue skies blue under **Natural** colours, and adds **Bright** (「明亮」), a third choice that
keeps the 0.4.1 look.

## Changed

### Three colour choices (all apps)

**Colours** (「顏色」) now offers three choices. A line under the picker says what the chosen one does.

| Choice | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Natural** (「自然」, the default) | Most colour. Light, vivid colours such as a blue sky come out a little darker to keep their colour. |
| **Bright** (「明亮」) | Keeps the photo's brightness. Light, vivid colours such as a blue sky lean white. This is Natural as it was in 0.4.0 and 0.4.1. |
| **Classic** (「經典」) | The original method, unchanged: lighter overall. Best for pictures already in the seven pure colours. |

- **Natural, before:** a light blue sky came out grey-white. The panel's blue ink is dark, so at the sky's brightness
  the panel could add only a few blue dots to white.
- **Natural, now:** blue skies look blue, and light greens, pinks and lavender get more colour too. Faint tints near
  white, skin tones and colours the panel can already show stay as they were. The strength was chosen on the device.
- **Grain:** changing from Classic to Natural or Bright sets **Grain** to **Standard**. Changing between Natural and
  Bright keeps your grain.
- With **Soft**, **Softer** and **Smoothest** grain, Natural shows bands of colour in a sky sooner than Bright.
- The command line (`ulani`, `ulani-swift`) takes `--colours natural|bright|classic`.

## Upgrading from 0.4.1

- **Your choice stays:** if you used Natural, you get the new Natural. Choose **Bright** for the 0.4.1 look.
- **What is already on the device stays as it is until you send it again:**
  - photo pages and cards: push them again;
  - calendar pages with a background: they change at their next sync.
- **Mac:**
  - Replace Paperhue in Applications. Your pages and settings are kept.
  - If macOS asks you to confirm the new download: **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
  - Open Paperhue once after updating. macOS asks once for each calendar source whether Paperhue may use it: enter
    your Mac's password and choose **Always Allow**.
  - The update stops the daily schedule for about half an hour, and macOS may show a crash report and "Paperhue can
    run in the background". The next time you open Paperhue or switch to it after that, it starts the schedule
    again. **Daily schedule…** shows when it last ran.
- **iPhone:** the web app updates itself. Reload it in Bluefy if it is still open.

## Download

- **Windows:** Paperhue.exe
- **Mac:** Paperhue-macOS.zip (macOS 14 or newer)
- **Android:** Paperhue-Android.apk
- **iPhone:** nothing to download. Open https://markhhm.github.io/ulani-epaper/ in the Bluefy browser.
